Great — thanks for the details, Alex. A few clarifications to avoid confusion on the unit-econ side and how we’ll price: 

1) Tokens vs characters vs requests: 
- Redwood bills on billed_tokens (prompt + completion) at the model/variant rate. Characters are a proxy: approximately 4 characters ~= 1 token (this varies by language/content). If you give us characters we’ll convert to tokens using that conversion for initial estimates and show sensitivity ranges.
- "Requests" is at the HTTP/API call level — each request can contain several prompts or tool calls and will incur billed tokens for everything sent/returned. So we need both requests/month and average tokens per request to compute cost.

2) Prompt caching vs billed tokens: 
- If many user prompts are repeated and we can apply prefix caching or response reuse, you can reduce billed tokens because we can return cached completions without re-running the model for identical prompts.
- Note: caching reduces billed tokens only when the cached response is served; control-plane/decision logic may still incur lightweight routing calls (usually negligible compared to full completions).

3) Example calculation (ballpark):
- Your 1,200 characters per user message -> ~300 tokens.
- If an average flow has prompt (300 tokens) + completion (200 tokens) = 500 billed tokens per model call.
- 1–2M user messages -> assuming 1.5 model calls average due to tool calls = 1.5 * 1.5M * 500 = ~1,125,000,000 billed tokens/month (~1.125B).
- At target pricing, to hit $2K–$6K/month, you’d need a unit cost of about $1.78–$5.33 per 1M tokens (which is below typical managed rates). With caching (say 50% effective), billed tokens drop proportionally.

We’ll run a few scenarios once we get your sample CSV. Also, if budget is strictly limited to $2K–$6K, we should discuss constrained approaches: stronger caching, smaller model variants for high-volume paths, and more aggressive batching.

I’ll draft a short scenario table and send by Friday. In the meantime, if you can confirm whether the 1–2M is active monthly users vs messages (we’ll treat as messages unless you correct us).

Best,
Marissa
